forbidden_overclaims: Do not claim exact ash depth, ash mass loading, or plume dispersion from this package alone.
Do not claim precise casualty, mortality, or loss totals beyond the report's limited statement.
Do not treat precipitation files as proof that lahars did or did not occur everywhere in the region.
Do not treat radar change as a direct lava or burn-scar map.
Do not infer official evacuation-zone geometry beyond the reported 20 km radius.

primary_gt.canonical_stance: The immediate response posture should prioritize near-field ashfall, evacuation, and air-quality management, with wet-ash/lahar access monitoring as a secondary watch.
forbidden_claims: Exact ash depth, ash mass loading, or plume dispersion values not supported by the task evidence.
Precise casualty, mortality, or loss totals beyond the limited report statement.
Definitive regional lahar occurrence or absence inferred only from precipitation context.
Radar change interpreted directly as a lava or burn-scar map.
Official evacuation-zone geometry beyond the reported 20 km radius.
primary_gt.rationale: Prioritize ashfall, evacuation, and air-quality management; keep wet-ash/lahar access monitoring as a secondary watch.
required_claims: Names ashfall, evacuation, and air-quality management as the dominant immediate priority.
Connects the priority to explosive eruption behavior, a high ash plume, and a second ash pulse.
Uses evacuation and nearby exposure indicators to justify life-safety and service-access urgency.
Places wet-ash/lahar route monitoring below the ashfall and evacuation priority.
Rejects lava or burn-scar image triage and ordinary weather response as weaker primary frames.

required_findings.finding: Treat explosive eruption behavior and high ash plume as the response driver.
Connect ashfall and plume exposure to evacuation, air quality, and nearby service/access concern.
Keep wet-ash/lahar route monitoring secondary rather than primary.

criteria.description: Selects ashfall, evacuation, and air-quality management as the highest-priority posture, using the canonical label or a clear semantic equivalent.
criteria.name: primary_priority_label

criteria.description: Ranks the postures as ashfall/evacuation/air quality first, wet-ash/lahar access monitoring second, lava or burn-scar image triage third, and ordinary weather response last.
criteria.name: priority_ranking

criteria.description: Includes the key numeric anchors within tolerance: plume at least 15 km, 1,500 to 2,000 evacuees, nearby population about 2,827, and 55 critical service amenities.
criteria.name: quantitative_anchors

criteria.description: Explains that explosive eruption behavior, a high ash plume, a second ash pulse, and near-field exposure drive evacuation and air-quality management.
criteria.name: eruption_mechanism_reasoning

criteria.description: Treats wet-ash and lahar-access monitoring as a secondary watch supported by precipitation, waterway, and road context, not as the dominant posture.
criteria.name: secondary_lahar_watch_logic

criteria.description: Rejects lava or burn-scar image triage as primary because image-change evidence is contextual, and rejects ordinary weather response because the event is an explosive volcanic crisis.
criteria.name: distractor_rejection

criteria.description: Avoids unsupported claims about exact ash depth or loading, exact losses, definitive lahar occurrence, radar-derived lava or burn scars, or official evacuation-zone geometry.
criteria.name: overclaim_control

criteria.description: Returns concise, well-formed JSON with answer, priority_rank, key_numeric_anchors, impact_chain, and rationale fields.
criteria.name: json_structure_and_concision

evidence_roles.image_change_context: situational context, not a lava or burn-scar primary decision
evidence_roles.masked_exposure_statistics: operational exposure context from derived package statistics
